When TESTING is on, exceptions get re-raised instead of being caught by the app's error handlers.
PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS is treated as true automatically whenever TESTING or DEBUG is enabled, unless you explicitly say otherwise.
SECRET_KEY is what Flask uses to sign session cookies, and it should never be shared publicly, like in commits or forum posts.
SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS lets you rotate keys without breaking existing sessions. Old keys should eventually be removed since each one adds a bit of overhead when checking signatures.
SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY is on by default, so JavaScript can't read the cookie. SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE is off by default, so the cookie can still be sent over plain HTTP unless you change that.
Turning on SESSION_COOKIE_PARTITIONED automatically turns on SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE too, since partitioned cookies only work over HTTPS.
MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH, MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE, and MAX_FORM_PARTS each cause a 413 error once their limit is crossed. Setting any of them to None turns that particular limit off.
TRUSTED_HOSTS gets checked during routing. If the host doesn't match, Flask raises a SecurityError, which shows up as a 400 response.
SERVER_NAME needs to be set if you're using subdomain matching, or if url_for has to build external URLs outside of a request.
The instance folder is meant to hold deployment specific files that shouldn't be checked into version control. If you pass instance_path yourself, it has to be an absolute path.
from_prefixed_env reads environment variables as JSON by default, so only lowercase true or false count as booleans. You can nest keys by separating them with double underscores.
